summary: which processors rach2/sys/proc/smp.c interrupts, through smp_hosttest.c, with five faults in a private copy of smp.c

argv: rm -rf ${WORK}/t && mkdir -p ${WORK}/t/tests/host && cp -R rach2 ${WORK}/t/ && cp -R ${SRC}/. ${WORK}/t/ && exec ${CC:-cc} -std=c99 -D_DEFAULT_SOURCE -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=0 -DRACH2_HOSTTEST -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -g -O1 -Wno-empty-body -ffreestanding -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/arch/x86 -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/arch/i686 -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib -I ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/proc -I utils -I krffs -I tests/host/compat -o ${WORK}/smp_hosttest tests/host/smp_hosttest.c ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib/kstring.c ${WORK}/t/rach2/sys/lib/kctypes.c

faults.name: no-skip
faults.summary: a shootdown that interrupts idle processors too

lines: smp-hosttest: fail: an idle processor that kept the directory is not interrupted and has it marked stale

faults.name: skip-all
faults.summary: a shootdown that passes every processor by, which leaves a running thread with a translation of a freed page

lines: smp-hosttest: fail: a processor that runs a thread of the directory is interrupted to drop the page

faults.name: no-release
faults.summary: a release that interrupts none, which leaves an idle processor on a freed directory

lines: smp-hosttest: fail: before a directory is freed, an idle processor that kept it gives it up for the kernel's

faults.name: no-stop-wait
faults.summary: a stop that does not wait for the processors it asks, which leaves one writing the log under the panic's record

lines: smp-hosttest: fail: and waits a second for the one that does not take it, none for those that do

faults.name: late-admit
faults.summary: a started processor that comes online whatever the boot decided, which leaves one online and uncounted

lines: smp-hosttest: fail: and one that comes after the wait stops, neither online nor counted
